To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

anti-TNF-alpha treatment of RA patients is associated with the downregulation of the expression of genes coding for calcium binding proteins and the upregulation of genes coding for ribosomal proteins and other genes involved in protein translation.

anti-TNF- α treatment of patients with rheumatic arthritis induces changes in the global gene expression in peripheral blood monocyte cells, including a downregulation of genes involved in inflammatory processes and an upregulation of genes implicated in protein synthesis.

the expression of several inflammatory genes, including those involved in the regulation of inflammation, immune response and apoptosis, are decreased in peripheral blood monocytes after anti-TNF-alpha treatment in responder RA patients.
